question: During which of the following movements did the extremists call for the boycott of British goods as a form of protest? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Swadeshi Movement
Civil Disobedience Movement
Non-Cooperation Movement
Quit India Movement
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Swadeshi Movement

Explanation:
The Swadeshi Movement (1905-1908) was launched in protest against the partition of Bengal. Extremists like Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, and Bipin Chandra Pal called for the boycott of British goods and promotion of indigenous products. The boycott aimed to exert economic pressure on the British government to reverse its policies. This movement marked a significant shift in the Indian freedom struggle as it involved mass participation and emphasized self-reliance. The Swadeshi Movement also promoted national education and cultural revival, making it a comprehensive protest against colonial rule.

☛ Date of Partition of Bengal → 16 October 1905
☛ Extremist leader of Swadeshi Movement → Bal Gangadhar Tilak
☛ Main objective of boycott → Economic pressure
☛ Outcome of the movement → Promotion of indigenous goods
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस आंदोलन के दौरान उग्रवादियों ने विरोध के रूप में ब्रिटिश वस्तुओं के बहिष्कार का आह्वान किया था? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है स्वदेशी आंदोलन

Explanation:
स्वदेशी आंदोलन (1905-1908) बंगाल के विभाजन के विरोध में शुरू हुआ। इसमें उग्रवादियों ने ब्रिटिश वस्तुओं के बहिष्कार, स्वदेशी वस्तुओं के उपयोग और राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा पर जोर दिया। इस आंदोलन का नेतृत्व बाल गंगाधर तिलक, लाला लाजपत राय और बिपिन चंद्र पाल जैसे उग्रवादी नेताओं ने किया। बहिष्कार का उद्देश्य आर्थिक दबाव डालकर ब्रिटिश सरकार को नीतियां बदलने के लिए मजबूर करना था। यह आंदोलन भारतीय स्वतंत्रता संग्राम में एक महत्वपूर्ण मोड़ था क्योंकि इसमें पहली बार व्यापक जनभागीदारी देखी गई और स्वदेशी वस्तुओं को बढ़ावा दिया गया।

question: Which of the following Governor-Generals introduced the General Service Enlistment Act? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Lord Auckland
Lord Amherst
Lord Wellesley
Lord Canning
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lord Canning

Explanation:
The General Service Enlistment Act was introduced in 1856 during the tenure of Lord Canning as Governor-General of India. This act required Indian soldiers to serve outside the country if needed when enlisted in the British Army. Previously, sepoys only agreed to serve within India. This act became a major cause of the Revolt of 1857, as sepoys saw it as a violation of their religious and social beliefs. Lord Canning served as Governor-General from 1856 to 1862 and played a key role in suppressing the revolt. The act increased dissatisfaction among Indian soldiers and marked a significant shift in British military policies in India.

☛ Year of enactment → 1856
☛ Impact of the Act → Sepoys had to serve abroad
☛ Result → Contributed to the 1857 Revolt
☛ Lord Canning's tenure → 1856-1862

question: Who among the following British officers introduced the policy of Subsidiary Alliance, one of the reason of 1857 revolt? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: John Nicholson
Sir Colin Campbell
Henry Lawrence
Lord Wellesley
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lord Wellesley

Explanation:
The policy of Subsidiary Alliance was introduced by Lord Wellesley (1798-1805). Under this policy, Indian states were required to maintain British troops and bear their expenses, leading to loss of independence. They lost control over foreign relations and accepted British supremacy. This policy brought many states under British control, causing discontent among local rulers. Economic exploitation and cultural interference further fueled public anger, contributing to the 1857 Revolt.

☛ Start of the revolt → 10 May 1857, Meerut

question: Which of the following Governor Generals of British India introduced the Permanent Settlement of Land Revenue in 1793? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Lord Warren Hastings
Lord Wellesley
Lord Cornwallis
Sir John Shore
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lord Cornwallis

Explanation:
The Permanent Settlement was introduced in 1793 by Lord Cornwallis. It was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa. This system granted zamindars the right to collect land revenue. The revenue rate was fixed permanently, ensuring a regular income for the Company. Zamindars were recognized as landowners, while peasants became tenants. The policy aimed to promote agricultural development and improve revenue management, but it led to increased exploitation of peasants. Cornwallis is also considered the father of the civil service in India.

☛ Where was Permanent Settlement implemented → Bengal, Bihar, Orissa
☛ Beneficiaries of Permanent Settlement → Zamindars
☛ Other reforms by Lord Cornwallis → Civil service, judicial reforms

question: What slogan did Lokmanya Tilak popularise regarding Swaraj? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: "Swaraj is achieved through sacrifice."
"Swaraj is given by the British."
"Swaraj is a gift."
"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it."
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.

Explanation:
Lokmanya Tilak popularised the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it', which energised the Indian freedom struggle. Tilak believed that Swaraj was not a gift or achieved through sacrifice, but was a birthright. This slogan is associated with the Home Rule Movement launched by Tilak and Annie Besant in 1916. Through this slogan, Tilak instilled a sense of self-respect and freedom among Indians. He was honored with the title 'Lokmanya' and started newspapers 'Kesari' in Marathi and 'Maratha' in English.

question: Who was the chief commissioner of Awadh in 1857? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Colville Coverly Jackson
Major John Sherbroke Banks
Major General Sir James Outram
Sir Henry Lawrence
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sir Henry Lawrence

Explanation:
At the time of the 1857 revolt, the Chief Commissioner of Awadh was Sir Henry Lawrence. He assumed the position after the annexation of Awadh in 1856 and commanded the British forces in Lucknow. During the revolt, he was besieged in the Lucknow Residency and was mortally wounded by a shell fragment on 4 July 1857. After his death, Major General Sir James Outram took over command. Sir Henry Lawrence is remembered for his military and administrative acumen, and his role in shaping British policy in Oudh.

question: Who fought in the famous Battle of Chinhat with the Britishers during the Revolt of 1857? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah
Rani Laxmibai
Maulana Azad
Shah Mal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah

Explanation:
The Battle of Chinhat was fought on 12 July 1857 near Lucknow during the Revolt of 1857. In this battle, Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah led the rebel forces against the British and defeated them. He was a prominent rebel leader from Faizabad, who fought against the British contingent commanded by Henry Lawrence. With the support of the Nawab of Nawabganj, Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah inflicted a heavy defeat on the British, forcing them to retreat. He continued to be a major threat to the British in the Awadh region until he was captured and executed on 5 June 1858.

question: What ideology did the extremists strongly oppose within the Indian National Congress? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 3)

Gradualism
Nationalism
Self-governance
solution:

Explanation:
The extremists within the Indian National Congress strongly opposed the policy of Gradualism (also known as the 'Slow and Steady' approach). The moderate leadership advocated for attaining self-governance through prayers, petitions, and gradual constitutional reforms. In contrast, the extremists demanded immediate complete Swaraj and considered the gradual approach ineffective. Led by leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, and Bipin Chandra Pal, they adopted aggressive methods including Swadeshi, boycott, and national education. The extremists believed that revolutionary steps were necessary to achieve freedom from British rule, rather than a slow process. Thus, gradualism was the primary ideology opposed by the extremists.

question: The British adopted which of the following policies with respect to landlords and zamindars after the Revolt of 1857? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 3)

The policy of confiscation of property
Policies that protected their rights and provided security over their lands
The policy of land redistribution
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Policies that protected their rights and provided security over their lands

Explanation:
After the Revolt of 1857, the British completely changed their administrative policy in India. They realized that zamindars and landlords had supported the revolt, but to ensure stability, they needed to win them over. Therefore, they adopted policies that protected the rights of zamindars and provided security over their lands. The aim was to create a loyal class that would support British rule. Under this policy, zamindars were given legal rights over their lands and were involved in local administration. This strengthened the zamindar class, increased pressure on peasants, and ensured the zamindars remained loyal to the British Crown. The policy was a strategic shift from earlier punitive measures to a more collaborative approach.

question: Tilak believed that political rights could only be achieved through: (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)

courageous action (strong pressure)
table talk
diplomatic discussions
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is courageous action (strong pressure)

Explanation:
Bal Gangadhar Tilak, popularly known as 'Lokmanya', was a prominent leader of the Indian freedom movement. He believed that political rights could only be achieved through courageous action and strong pressure against the British rule. Tilak advocated for aggressive nationalism and emphasized mass mobilization and resistance. He coined the famous slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright' and launched the Home Rule Movement in 1916. He opposed the policy of negotiation or compromise and considered direct action essential. Tilak was also a journalist and ran two newspapers, Kesari (Marathi) and Maratha (English), to spread nationalist ideas. His leadership greatly influenced the radical wing of the Indian National Congress.

question: The Moderates' demand for 'No taxation without representation' was inspired by which historical movement? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Chinese Revolution
Russian Revolution
French Revolution
American War of Independence
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is American War of Independence

Explanation:
The Moderates of the Indian National Congress, such as Dadabhai Naoroji, Ferozeshah Mehta, and Gopal Krishna Gokhale, were inspired by the American War of Independence when they raised the demand of 'No taxation without representation'. This slogan was originally used by American colonists in 1765 to protest against the Stamp Act imposed by the British Parliament. The Moderates wanted Indians to have representation in the British Parliament so that taxes could not be levied without their consent. Their approach was constitutional and based on appeals to British justice and gradual reforms. The American struggle for representation against arbitrary taxation served as a historical precedent for their demand.

question: Which of the following Acts introduced the bicameral system of legislature in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Simon Commission, 1927
Government of India Act, 1935
Indian Independence Act, 1947
Government of India Act, 1919
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1919

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced the bicameral system of legislature in India. Under this Act, the central legislature was divided into two houses: the Council of State (upper house) and the Central Legislative Assembly (lower house). This Act was based on the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, which also introduced the dyarchy system in provinces. However, the bicameral system was implemented only at the central level; provincial legislatures remained unicameral. This Act was a significant step in the evolution of the Indian constitution.

question: Who is credited with starting the rumour about cartridges coated with cow and pig fat, which resulted in the outbreak of the First War of Independence in India in 1857? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)

A low-caste khalasi working in Dum Dum
A Brahmin priest
A British officer
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A low-caste khalasi working in Dum Dum

Explanation:
The rumour that the new Enfield rifle cartridges were greased with cow and pig fat was started by a low-caste khalasi (labourer) working at the Dum Dum arsenal. This rumour deeply offended both Hindu and Muslim sepoys, as cows were sacred to Hindus and pigs were considered unclean by Muslims. The khalasi reportedly shared this information with a Brahmin sepoy, who then spread it further. British officials attempted to quash the rumour by investigating, but by then it had already caused widespread anger. This incident is considered the immediate spark of the 1857 rebellion. Thus, a low-caste khalasi from Dum Dum is credited with originating the rumour.

question_hi: 1857 में भारत के प्रथम स्वतंत्रता संग्राम के प्रकोप के परिणामस्वरूप गाय और सूअर की चर्बी से लेपित कारतूसों के बारे में अफवाह फैलाने का श्रेय किसे दिया जाता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: एक सिपाही कमांडर
दमदम में काम करने वाला एक निम्न जाति का खलासी

एक ब्रिटिश अधिकारी
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है दमदम में काम करने वाला एक निम्न जाति का खलासी

Explanation:
1857 के विद्रोह की शुरुआत में एक निम्न जाति के खलासी ने दमदम में काम करते हुए यह अफवाह फैलाई कि नई एनफील्ड राइफल के कारतूस गाय और सूअर की चर्बी से लेपित हैं। हिंदू सैनिकों के लिए गाय पवित्र थी, जबकि मुस्लिम सैनिक सूअर को अशुद्ध मानते थे। इस अफवाह से दोनों समुदायों में आक्रोश फैल गया। यह घटना दमदम में ब्रिटिश सेना की छावनी में हुई थी, जहाँ इस खलासी ने एक ब्राह्मण सिपाही से बात करते समय यह दावा किया। बाद में ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों ने जाँच की, लेकिन तब तक अफवाह फैल चुकी थी और बड़े पैमाने पर विद्रोह भड़क गया। इस प्रकार, एक निचली जाति के खलासी को इस अफवाह का प्रारंभिक स्रोत माना जाता है।
